summary: The Definition Unit Tests (Condition C) method is effective. On both base models, C improves main accuracy over the engagement-matched neutral-checks baseline (B) by a statistically significant margin, and C > B holds in all 3 convention families.

primary_criterion.description: C improves main accuracy over B by >= 5pp (or paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0) on BOTH models, AND C > B in >= 2 of 3 families

c_vs_a.description: Does DUT improve over plain glossary injection?

qwen25_math_7b.note: Asymptotics tied at 99%. Largest gain in completeness (+11pp).

llama31_8b.note: Convolution tied at 66%. Largest gain in completeness (+52pp) and asymptotics (+22pp).

c_vs_majority_vote.description: Does single-sample DUT outperform 5-sample majority vote?

qwen25_math_7b.note: C massively outperforms majority vote. A@5 and B@5 degraded by shorter max_tokens (512 vs 2048).

llama31_8b.note: C significantly outperforms majority vote on Llama as well.

alternate_convention_reduction.description: Does C reduce alternate-convention match rate?

decision_rule_applied.rule: Proceed if both models show C > B by >= 5pp (or CI excluding 0) AND C > B in >= 2/3 families. Pivot if only 1 family. Refute if C <= B on both models.
decision_rule_applied.justification: On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, C - B = +5.0pp (CI [+2.0%, +8.3%]), C > B in 3/3 families. On Llama-3.1-8B, C - B = +22.7pp (CI [+16.0%, +29.3%]), C > B in 3/3 families. Both models exceed the 5pp threshold with CIs excluding zero. The engagement-matched control (B) rules out the extra-computation confound: B performs comparably to A (Qwen: -0.3pp; Llama: +2.0pp), while C provides a large additional boost.
